newsitem.title: JAPAN: False alarm stirs damaged Japan nuclear facility.
newsitem.headline: False alarm stirs damaged Japan nuclear facility.

text.p: A false alarm caused a temporary alert on Monday at a nuclear fuel reprocessing facility that was the site last week of Japan's worst nuclear accident, officials said.

Alarms indicating that radioactive substances at the plutonium fuel plant at the facility had reached a critical point went off briefly at 9:01 a.m (0001 GMT), said an official at the state-run Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), owner of the plant.
About 30 minutes later, PNC officials determined the signal, which indicated that nuclear materials could begin continuous nuclear fission reactions, was a false alarm.
The false alarm was the latest in a string of incidents to underscore security concerns about the plant since March 11, when a fire and explosion exposed 37 workers to low-level radiation.
The alarm went off at a location in the sprawling complex in Tokaimura, 160 km (100 miles) northeast of Tokyo, separate from the fire and explosion.
On Sunday the PNC acknowledged it did not alert a group of students and foreign trainees who were touring the facility on the day the fire broke out to any possible danger.
The 64 people who toured the plant were not informed of the dangers and were not checked for exposure to radiation, a PNC official said.
Investigation of the accident has revealed lapses in safety standards, including outdated firefighting equipment and delays in alerting both residents and central authorities of the crisis.
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto last week apologised to the nation and called for an investigation into the accident and subsequent lapses.
